# v1.0.14 — archival metadata aligned with the revised manuscript title

This release aligns the archived bibliographic metadata with the revised
manuscript title. The title now reports the principal finding rather than a
normative recommendation. No analysis artefact changes.

## What changed

- `.zenodo.json`: title, `version` (v1.0.14) and a new change-log paragraph.
- `CITATION.cff`: title and `version` (1.0.14); the `doi` field keeps the concept
  DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23677282, which always resolves to the latest version.
- `README.md`: header title and a new "Version 1.0.14" section. Earlier version
  notes are kept as historical records.

## What did not change

- No script, estimate, exhibit, figure or `run_all.sh` step.
- No CHARLS microdata; the repository guard `tools/check_no_microdata.py` should
  be run on every changed file before the commit.
- The concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23677282 is unchanged.

## Note for the manuscript

The version DOI is allocated when Zenodo archives this release. After publication,
record it in the manuscript's Availability of data and materials statement and in
reference 57, and in the quoted Code availability block of `DATA_AVAILABILITY.md`.
The helper `回填_v1014.py <new-version-doi>` in the submission package performs
these replacements and verifies that the old version DOI is gone. The resulting
`DATA_AVAILABILITY.md` update is a main-branch documentation commit and does not
change the tagged v1.0.14 snapshot.

Zenodo's GitHub integration archives this release under the existing concept DOI;
the title of the new record must be:

Reproducibility package for 'Two-year agreement of a low handgrip strength classification in 9116 Chinese adults: reproduction is lowest near the cut-off'
